question.problem: If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{100}$ is a sample of size $n=100$ drawn from a population with mean $\mu =30$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=9,$ calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

Since the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=9$ and the sample size $n=100,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}] & =\frac{9}{100} \\  & =0.09.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{0.09}=0.3.
$$
